title: Securely accessing an Azure OpenAI model from an Azure Logic Apps Standard AI agent using a Private Endpoint.
summary: Azure Logic Apps Standard can securely connect to Azure OpenAI through a private endpoint without public internet exposure. The post explains how to configure a virtual network with subnets, create a private endpoint for Azure OpenAI, disable public access, enable VNet integration on Logic Apps, and use managed identity authentication instead of API keys.
key_points: Private endpoint creates a private network interface for Azure OpenAI accessible via a private IP within the VNet
Logic Apps Standard requires VNet integration with subnet delegation to route outbound traffic privately
System-assigned managed identity replaces API key authentication, following least privilege with Cognitive Services OpenAI User role
DNS resolution within VNet returns the private IP, while external traffic sees public IP which is disabled after setup
All traffic flows through Microsoft backbone network infrastructure, never reaching the public internet

quotes.text: All traffic flows privately. No data traverses the public internet.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the security goal achieved by the architecture described
